B2csOut.description:
One aggregated B2C-small figure: place of supply x rate x inter/intra-state.

Aggregated because that is what the return declares — B2CS is not invoice-wise. Credit notes
to unregistered buyers below the B2CL threshold net in here with their sign, so the figure
can legitimately be negative in a heavy-returns month.
B2csOut.title: B2csOut

CustomerOut.description: A billed party. `id` is the finance customer id invoices and payments reference.
CustomerOut.title: CustomerOut

CustomerSummary.description: One row of the customers ledger: the party plus their receivable position.
CustomerSummary.title: CustomerSummary

CustomerUpdate.description:
PATCH: every field optional, only what is sent is applied
(`model_dump(exclude_unset=True)`); everything else is validated exactly as on create.
CustomerUpdate.title: CustomerUpdate

DocumentSeriesOut.description:
One declared document series — the numbers issued and how many were cancelled.

The one section a **void** belongs in: its figures are not a supply, but its number was
consumed, and a gap in a series is how an unreported invoice announces itself.
DocumentSeriesOut.title: DocumentSeriesOut

EInvoiceFilingOut.description:
One recorded attempt to register a document with the Invoice Registration Portal.

Append-only: this is a row of history, never a mutable status. A retry is a further row.
EInvoiceFilingOut.title: EInvoiceFilingOut

EInvoiceState.description:
An invoice's *current* e-invoice position, derived from its newest filing row.

Carried on the invoice read model so a screen never has to fetch the history to know whether
a document is registered. `required` is the statutory question (B2B, export and SEZ documents
need an IRN; B2C does not), and it is answered even when nothing has been attempted — that is
what makes an un-filed obligation visible instead of silent.
EInvoiceState.title: EInvoiceState

EwayBillOut.description: One recorded attempt to raise an e-Way bill. Append-only: a retry is a further row.
EwayBillOut.title: EwayBillOut

EwayBillWithInvoice.description: One bill on a list page, with enough of its document to be recognisable.
EwayBillWithInvoice.title: EwayBillWithInvoice

EwayState.description:
A document's *current* e-Way position, derived from its newest attempt.

Never null on a document that needs a bill: an unmet obligation must be **visible** rather
than absent, which is the same reason `EInvoiceState.required` exists.
EwayState.title: EwayState

FileReturnIn.description: Record that a generated return went to the portal, with the ARN it came back with.
FileReturnIn.title: FileReturnIn

GenerateReturnIn.description:
Assemble one period's return from the invoices already recorded.

Generating twice replaces the snapshot with what the book says *now* and appends a second
`generated` transition, which is the honest answer before filing. After filing it is refused
— a filed return is what was reported, and the remedy for a later correction is the diff.
GenerateReturnIn.title: GenerateReturnIn

GstRegistrationOut.description: The organization's own GST registration — who this seller is, to the portal.
GstRegistrationOut.title: GstRegistrationOut

GstRegistrationUpsert.description:
Register or update this organization's GSTIN. The number is parsed and checksum-verified
before a row is written — an unverified GSTIN is not stored anywhere in this service.
GstRegistrationUpsert.title: GstRegistrationUpsert

GstReturnDetail.description:
The return with its sections and its whole status trail.

`sections` is null on a `draft` — a period nobody has assembled has nothing to declare, and
an empty return and an unassembled one are different answers. Which concrete shape it is —
`Gstr1Sections` or `Gstr3bSections` — follows `ret.return_type`; `selectors.return_detail`
picks the validator, since the two tables share nothing a discriminator could read.
GstReturnDetail.title: GstReturnDetail

GstReturnOut.description: One period's return: the record, not the snapshot. What a list page renders.
GstReturnOut.title: GstReturnOut

GstReturnTransitionOut.description: One movement between statuses — a row of the append-only trail.
GstReturnTransitionOut.title: GstReturnTransitionOut

Gstr1Sections.description:
Every section of one GSTR-1, and the shape the snapshot is stored in.

This *is* the persisted JSONB on `gst_returns.sections`, validated on the way in and on the
way out, so a snapshot written by an older revision cannot be served back as something the
contract no longer describes.
Gstr1Sections.title: Gstr1Sections

Gstr3bItcOut.description:
Table 4, in the shape Notification 14/2022-CT gave it — see `domain.Gstr3bItc`.

4A(5) is **gross**, including credit blocked under s. 17(5); 4B splits the reversal the return
itself asks for; 4C is the net the ledger actually carries forward; 4D is informational and
always zero — neither a Rule 37 re-claim nor a s. 16(4)/place-of-supply ineligibility is
modelled.
Gstr3bItcOut.title: Gstr3bItcOut

Gstr3bOutwardOut.description:
Table 3.1. Only (a) and (b) are ever non-zero — see `domain.Gstr3bOutward` for why (c),
(d) and (e) are always zero given what this platform records today. `outward_reverse_charge`
is not a numbered row of the form; it is the taxable value of an outward reverse-charge supply
this organization raised, kept visible and excluded from (a) because the recipient, not this
organization, owes the tax on it.
Gstr3bOutwardOut.title: Gstr3bOutwardOut

Gstr3bPaymentOut.description:
Table 6.1 — the liability, how credit covered it, and what is left for cash. Late fee and
interest are out of scope for this slice; see the README.
Gstr3bPaymentOut.title: Gstr3bPaymentOut

Gstr3bSections.description:
Every table of one GSTR-3B, and the shape the snapshot is stored in — the `gstr3b` analogue
of `Gstr1Sections`.
Gstr3bSections.title: Gstr3bSections

HsnSummaryOut.description:
One row of the HSN summary. A line with no code groups under a null rather than vanishing:
a missing classification is a gap the return must show, not one it should quietly close.
HsnSummaryOut.title: HsnSummaryOut

ImsDecisionCreate.description:
Record a decision on one inbound document. Append-only: a change of mind is a further row,
never an edit, because the question asked later is what was decided *and when*.
ImsDecisionCreate.title: ImsDecisionCreate

ImsDecisionOut.description:
One operator's decision on one inbound document — a row of history, never a status.

Carries what the platform suggested *at the time*, so "did the operator follow the machine"
stays answerable after a later run changes the current suggestion.
ImsDecisionOut.title: ImsDecisionOut

ImsDocumentDetail.description:
One inbound document with the evidence behind its suggestion.

The evidence is the point of the detail view: an operator asked to accept or reject somebody
else's claim needs to see the document it was matched to, or the earlier copy it duplicates,
or the absence of either — not a verdict.
ImsDocumentDetail.title: ImsDocumentDetail

ImsDocumentOut.description:
One row of the reconciliation queue.

`status` is where the document stands — `pending` until somebody decides. `suggestion` is the
newest advice and is null only before the first reconciliation run has seen the document;
`decision` is the newest decision, and null is what "nobody has decided yet" looks like.
ImsDocumentOut.title: ImsDocumentOut

ImsSuggestion.description:
What the platform proposes for one inbound document, and why.

`reason` is the field a queue is worked by: "matched exactly" and "the supplier declares 500
paise more than the purchase order" need entirely different attention, and a queue showing
only an action makes the operator re-derive the reason for every row.
ImsSuggestion.title: ImsSuggestion

InvoiceIssueIn.description:
The principal route's own contract for issuing an invoice or a credit note.

Deliberately **not** `InvoiceCreate`: that schema carries `number` and `status`, and a public
caller may set neither. The server owns the numbering series
(`services.allocate_invoice_number`, race-safe per organization/document-type/financial-year)
and the lifecycle status is always derived — there is no draft -> issued transition and no way
to force `paid` or `void` through this route. Unknown fields are rejected rather than silently
ignored.
InvoiceIssueIn.title: InvoiceIssueIn

InvoiceLineOut.description:
One line on an invoice. `amount_minor` foots to `quantity x unit_price_minor`, and is the
**taxable value** the line's GST is computed on.

Exactly one tax shape is populated: `cgst_minor` + `sgst_minor` on an intra-state supply,
`igst_minor` on an inter-state one. The three always sum to the tax actually charged.
InvoiceLineOut.title: InvoiceLineOut

InvoiceOut.description:
An invoice or credit note. Totals foot exactly:
`subtotal_minor = Σ line.amount_minor`, `total_minor = subtotal_minor + tax_minor`,
and `tax_minor = cgst_minor + sgst_minor + igst_minor = Σ line tax`.
A credit note carries negative amounts and a `corrects_invoice_id`.
InvoiceOut.title: InvoiceOut

InvoiceWithholdingOut.description:
One deduction or collection on one document — a row of the register.

`rate_pct` and `threshold_minor` are **snapshots** of the version named by
`withholding_rate_id`, not a live read of the schedule: a rate change must not restate a
figure somebody has already been paid net of.
InvoiceWithholdingOut.title: InvoiceWithholdingOut

ItcBalanceOut.description:
The ITC ledger's position for one registration as of one period — the figure Table 6.1
utilises on top of the period's own net eligible credit.
ItcBalanceOut.title: ItcBalanceOut

ItcHeadBalanceOut.description:
One tax head's position for one period: what accrued, what reversed, what was consumed,
and the balance carried forward — `sum(amount_minor)` up to and including this period.
ItcHeadBalanceOut.title: ItcHeadBalanceOut

ItcLedgerEntryOut.description:
One posting to the input-tax-credit ledger. Append-only: `accrual`, `reversal` or
`utilisation` — never an edit to an earlier row.
ItcLedgerEntryOut.title: ItcLedgerEntryOut

OverviewKpi.description: A headline KPI for the overview, pre-derived from the ledger.
OverviewKpi.title: OverviewKpi

OverviewSummary.description: Everything the Overview screen needs, in one payload.
OverviewSummary.title: OverviewSummary

PaymentAllocationOut.description: How much of a received payment was applied to one invoice.
PaymentAllocationOut.title: PaymentAllocationOut

PaymentOut.description: A payment received from a customer, split across one or more invoices.
PaymentOut.title: PaymentOut

PurchaseDocumentCreate.description:
Record what a supplier billed. The tax split is **computed**, never supplied: the service
derives CGST/SGST/IGST from the taxable value and the rate with the same `domain.split_gst`
an invoice uses, so the purchase book and the sales book cannot disagree about arithmetic.
PurchaseDocumentCreate.title: PurchaseDocumentCreate

PurchaseDocumentOut.description: A recorded purchase or expense document — the local counterpart of a supplier's filing.
PurchaseDocumentOut.title: PurchaseDocumentOut

RateGroupOut.description: One rate group inside a section — the grain GSTR-1 is actually declared at.
RateGroupOut.title: RateGroupOut

ReturnDiffOut.description:
What has changed since the return was generated — never a rewrite of the return.

The whole reason a generated return is frozen. An invoice corrected after August was filed
does not make August a different return; it makes a **difference**, which is what an
amendment in a later period declares. This endpoint is that difference, per section and in
total, so the amendment is prepared from an answer rather than from a memory.
ReturnDiffOut.title: ReturnDiffOut

ReturnInvoiceOut.description: One document as B2B, B2CL, CDNR, CDNUR or EXP declares it: header plus rate groups.
ReturnInvoiceOut.title: ReturnInvoiceOut

ReturnTotalsOut.description: The return's one-line declaration. Every section sums to exactly this.
ReturnTotalsOut.title: ReturnTotalsOut

SectionDeltaOut.description: How one section moved between the snapshot and the book as it stands now.
SectionDeltaOut.title: SectionDeltaOut

TaxHeadAmountsOut.description:
An amount broken across the four heads GST is payable under. `cess_minor` is carried for
forward compatibility and is always zero today — see `domain.TaxHeadAmounts`.
TaxHeadAmountsOut.title: TaxHeadAmountsOut

UtilisationLineOut.description: One application of credit against liability — see `domain.utilise_itc`.
UtilisationLineOut.title: UtilisationLineOut

WithholdingDeductorRow.description:
One counterparty's line in the GSTR-7-style summary.

GSTR-7 is declared **per deductor**: the number they hold, the value they deducted against,
and the three heads. Grouping the register that way is what makes the platform's figures
comparable to the return the deductor actually files — which is the reconciliation a supplier
does, and the reason this summary exists on the receivable side at all.
WithholdingDeductorRow.title: WithholdingDeductorRow

WithholdingRateOut.description: One version of one withholding head. Global vocabulary, versioned by `effective_from`.
WithholdingRateOut.title: WithholdingRateOut

WithholdingSummaryOut.description:
One period's withholding, grouped the way the return declares it, and footed.

`total_*` sums the rows exactly; a test asserts it, because a summary that does not foot to
its own rows is worse than no summary.
WithholdingSummaryOut.title: WithholdingSummaryOut

WithholdingWithInvoice.description: One register row on a list page, with enough of its document to be recognisable.
WithholdingWithInvoice.title: WithholdingWithInvoice

put.description:
Configuration, not a document — the one write here that overwrites rather than appends.

A registration is configuration, so it is idempotent on the GSTIN and
updates in place. What it must never do is rewrite history — an invoice already filed keeps
the `seller_gstin` it was filed under, because that column is a snapshot on the invoice and
not a join to here.

itself has. The snapshot is not here — it is opened, not scrolled past.

post.description:
Generate the return and freeze the snapshot.

A 201 whether or not the record already existed, because what is created either way is the
snapshot — the return record is only the box it lives in. Refused outright on a **filed**
period: the snapshot is what was reported, and regenerating over it would erase the only
record of what the filing actually said.

get.description:
The return as it was assembled — the snapshot, not a re-derivation.

Serving the stored sections rather than re-assembling on read is the whole point of freezing
them: this is what was reported, and it must keep saying so after the book moves underneath
it. What the book says *now* is a different question, answered by the diff endpoint.
get.summary: One return, with every section and its whole status trail

get.description:
The difference, per section and in total, between the snapshot and the book as it stands.

A credit note raised in September against an August invoice does not make August a different
return; it makes a difference, and a difference is what an amendment in a later period
declares. This is that difference, so the amendment is prepared from an answer rather than
from somebody's memory of what August looked like.

post.description:
Mark the return filed. Behind its own dangerous permission, and terminal.

A POST to a `filing` sub-collection rather than a PATCH of `status`, for the same reason IMS
decisions are a collection: this appends a row to a trail that is never rewritten, and the
verb should say so.

Grouped per deductor, because that is how GSTR-7 is declared — which is what makes these
figures comparable to the return the deductor actually files, and therefore reconcilable.
get.summary: One period's withholding grouped per counterparty — the GSTR-7 shape

get.description:
The queue, filtered the way it is actually worked.

Every filter answers a question somebody asks out loud — "what is still undecided", "August",
"everything from this supplier", "show me only the mismatches" — and `reason` is the one that
makes the queue tractable: it filters on the newest suggestion, so an operator can take the
exact matches in one pass and give the disagreements the attention they need.

Oldest first by default, because a queue is worked forward: the document closest to its return
deadline matters more than the one that arrived most recently.

get.description:
The document, its newest suggestion, what that suggestion was based on, and every decision
recorded against it.

The evidence is the whole point of the detail view. An operator asked to accept or reject
somebody else's claim on this business needs to see the purchase document it was matched to,
or the earlier copy it duplicates, or the absence of both — a verdict on its own is something
they can only take on trust, and trust is not what a compliance queue is for.
get.summary: One inbound supplier document, with the evidence behind its suggestion

post.description:
Record what a person decided — append-only, with who and when.

A POST rather than a PUT, and a `decisions` collection rather than a `status` field, because
that is what this is: a decision is appended to a history, never written over the last one. A
change of mind is a further row, and the row that was superseded stays visible with the
correction after it — which is the same shape invoices and filings already have, and the
reason GST's own model fits this platform without adaptation.

Behind its own permission, marked dangerous: accepting claims the input tax credit on the
document and rejecting declines it. Reading the queue and deciding it are different jobs.
post.summary: Accept, reject or park one inbound supplier document

get.summary: What this service is
Invoices and credit notes

post.description:
Finalize a new document. There is no edit, delete, void or draft -> issued transition —
the only legitimate corrections are a credit note (this same route, `document_type` =
`credit_note` and `corrects_invoice_id` set) and, for an e-invoiced document, an IRN
cancellation inside its 24-hour window.

The number is never taken from the caller: the server allocates the next one in this
organization's own series (`services.allocate_invoice_number`), so a duplicate is
structurally impossible rather than merely checked for. The lifecycle status is always
derived, never forced — `InvoiceIssueIn` carries no `status` field at all.
post.summary: Issue an invoice, or a credit note against one

post.description:
Ask for another attempt at a bill, without waiting for the automatic retry (C4).

**202, not 201**: this stages a request and returns; the portal call happens afterwards, in the
worker, on the same claim/call/record path the automatic retry uses (D3 — a route wrapped end
to end by the tenant transaction must never hold it open across a government's answer). The
response is the document's e-Way position as it stands now; poll it, or read the
`retry_scheduled` / `generated` / `failed` events.

Offered for an outage still awaiting its retry and for a failed generation whose cause was the
platform's (`retry_exhausted`, `stale`, `no_registration`) — `EwayState.can_retry` says which.
A portal **refusal** is a 409 naming the code and what to fix: the identical consignment would
be refused again. Rate limited per document.

404.description: That invoice is not part of this organization

409.description: Nothing to retry: a bill already stands, a generation is in flight, or the portal refused the consignment and would refuse it again

429.description: Retried too recently — one attempt per document per few seconds

get.summary: Liveness — is the process up?

get.description:
How far behind the relay is. **Alert on `oldest_seconds`.**

A stalled relay is the platform's quietest failure. It selects, finds nothing,
logs nothing, sleeps, and loops — `attempts` never increments and `last_error`
stays null, so the process looks healthy indefinitely while the outbox grows
without bound and every consumer downstream starves.

Deliberately **not** part of readiness. A backlog is not a reason to take the
service out of rotation: refusing traffic would stop new events being written
without helping drain the ones already queued, which makes the incident worse.
This is a metric to alert on, not a health state.

Counted through the outbox engine, not the application one. The app role is
NOBYPASSRLS and this request binds no tenant, so through it `pending` would be
zero whatever the table holds — the probe that exists to expose the stall would
be wired to the same blind spot that causes it.
get.summary: Outbox depth and age — scrape this

get.description:
Route traffic on this; restart on /health.

Conflating the two restarts a healthy process that is merely waiting on a
dependency.

Only the dependencies a service actually declares are checked. A gateway owns no
tables, so asking it for a database is asking a question whose answer means nothing
— and a readiness probe that reports on something the service does not use is worse
than no probe, because it will eventually fail for a reason nobody can act on.
get.summary: Readiness — can it serve traffic?

get.description:
Reachable only on the compose `back` network (`tests/infra`'s
`test_metrics_never_routed.py` is the lint that keeps it that way) — never behind
Caddy or a gateway, the same rule `ops_monitor`'s own `/metrics` follows.

`db_pool_in_use` is always reported when this service has a database; the three
outbox gauges only when `outbox_model` is configured — same gate as `/health/outbox`,
and the same reason: an app-role connection with no tenant bound sees zero rows.
